sections.overview: This bottom-dwelling dragonet ranges through the north-east Atlantic and Mediterranean, from Norway and the North Sea south to Mauritania and the western Black Sea.
sections.identification: Its flattened triangular head and upward-facing eyes are distinctive; breeding males have an unusually tall first dorsal fin and vivid blue lines, unlike the smaller, dark-spotted C. maculatus.
sections.habitat: Adults live on sandy or shell-gravel seabeds from shallow coastal water to several hundred metres, often partly buried, while juveniles may occur in shallow tidal pools.
sections.diet: It eats benthic invertebrates; a British gut-content study found crustaceans dominant, especially porcelain crabs, with polychaete worms as a supplementary prey.
sections.behavior: The fish can bury itself rapidly in sand, and territorial males display and court females with a conspicuous spread of their dorsal fins.
sections.reproduction: Courtship includes a paired rise toward the surface, where eggs and sperm are released; the eggs and larvae remain pelagic, with spawning reported in spring and summer.
sections.ecology: It belongs to Callionymidae, the dragonets; the closely compared C. maculatus can be separated by rows of dark flank spots, a useful distinction when females and juveniles are less colourful.
sections.conservation: Regional accounts describe its ecology but report no global IUCN threat category for the species.
